title: 30-storey tower approved near Allen ION station
subtitle: Council also delegated severe-weather declarations, amended traffic and parking rules, and set the 2024 meeting schedule.
overview: Council approved Official Plan Amendment No. 39 and a zoning change for 203-207 King Street South and 10-16 John Street West in Uptown. The proposal is a 24-storey tower on a six-storey podium with retail and a daycare at street level. It exceeds the height and density now permitted, and the vote was {{vote:m7}}. Council asked the Region of Waterloo to approve the plan amendment.

Staff said the site is next to an ION station and in the city's primary growth area. Council members cited the housing shortage as the deciding factor. Nearby residents raised concerns about shadows, wind, traffic, deliveries, setbacks and the notice they received. Council also asked staff to look again at loading and deliveries during site plan review.

On the consent agenda, Council gave the Chief Administrative Officer authority to declare a Significant Weather Event, which matters for winter road maintenance. It also amended the Traffic and Parking By-law and approved the 2024 Council meeting schedule. Council met in closed session earlier in the day on legal advice about a settlement and on housing matters. The minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the plan amendment, asked the Region to approve it, and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-11 for the King Street South and John Street West tower {{vote:m7}}.

Council delegated authority to declare a Significant Weather Event under the Minimum Maintenance Standards to the Chief Administrative Officer or designate, and directed staff to bring forward an amending by-law.
Council approved report IPPW2023-045 and amended Traffic and Parking By-law 08-077 for various locations.
Council approved the proposed 2024 Council meeting schedule set out in Appendix A of report CORP2023-044.

debate: Supporters, including staff and several delegates, said the site is next to an ION station and in the primary growth area. They argued that the housing shortage and low vacancy justify added height and density. A delegate for the applicant said the tower was made slimmer and taller to add bedrooms and two-bedroom units.

Residents of neighbouring buildings said the tower would shade them, especially in winter mornings. They also said it would worsen wind already felt around nearby buildings. Staff and the applicant said the studies met the city's urban design criteria and showed no adverse wind impacts at street level. One councillor said the wind study showed a minor improvement on John Street.

Delegates said Caroline and John Streets already have double-parked delivery trucks and construction trades parking. They said the traffic study did not look at access to individual properties. Staff said visitor parking and loading meet zoning rules and that John Street's temporary parking limits would be reviewed.

Several delegates objected to reduced setbacks and a density well above what the zoning by-law sets. Staff said the tower separation from the neighbouring building is well above the minimum. They also said the street-side setbacks suit an urban area.

Some residents said they received notice only a day or two before the deadline for registering as a delegate. Staff said the comment period was still open and that the city is updating its notification practices after a local newspaper stopped delivery.
